summary:
Done. When a turn ends while the octopus is upstairs with the player, it now stays there, awake and visible, until the player goes down (OW-3, option b, the owner default of 11-13). Going down by any route puts it on the attic blanket with at least the minimum awake time left (AWAKE_SEEN, 15 s), and it then naps as usual. Climbing again during that window does not bring it back up. The octopus is never asleep upstairs: whenever it has to fall asleep while it is up there (another tab's turn arrives after the window has passed, the test hook __ppolAwakeMs is 0, or the window simply runs out), sleepNow moves it to the blanket first, which is the old move. OW-4 (the window only counts while the attic is in view) is unchanged and is now written down as a decision.

The fix is 9 changed lines in js/app.js. Scenario Z part 5 was rewritten and extended, and the two missing weekly checks RO-1 and RO-2 were added to Q21. Every new or rewritten check fails when its line of the fix is reverted; the mutation table is below.

Suites on the final code: npm test all green; font check `stale: none`; Z passed three runs in a row (54/0 each); Q passed three runs in a row (64/0 each); A 74/0; Y 99/0 on the rerun (the first Y run stopped on an unrelated dialog wait under load, see suites). I did not commit anything.

This session continued an earlier run that a container restart stopped. That run had finished the code, the tests, the mutants, the pictures and every suite except a clean Y. I read its notes and the diff, reviewed the code paths again, reran Y and the font check, and wrote this report.

changes.what: When the octopus comes down from upstairs (octUnmountLoft emits octUp(false, anchor)) and the app is in a rest phase (restPhase() !== 'up'), it is placed on the blanket: `if (an !== 'blanket' && restPhase() !== 'up') octPlace('blanket')`.
changes.why: This is the one place every route out of the loft passes through: the stairs, showPlace for the play room or the outside, a ceremony start, and finishing the salon. The move happens behind the down transition, so the player never sees it. The window was frozen upstairs (rest.away), so restTick gives back at least AWAKE_SEEN once the attic is in view again.

A sleeping octopus is always on the blanket. Every path into sleep (lieDown with or without a watcher, the armRest(t, 0) hook, the 6 s guard) goes through sleepNow, so moving it to the blanket there covers them all. lieDown upstairs while watching resolves walkTo at once (the scene does not walk upstairs) and calls sleepNow(t) without place; that call now also moves it down.

changes.what: Comment updated for 11-13. restDown itself is unchanged.
changes.why: restDown now runs only when the octopus goes to sleep.

Another tab's turn end, or this tab becoming visible, inside the window: the octopus stays upstairs. Outside the window, the existing armRest(t, 0) leads to lieDown and sleepNow, which moves it to the blanket asleep.

changes.what: Removed `restDown()` from `stopWander(); restDown();`; updated the comments on the hook-0 line and the walkTo('blanket') line.
changes.why: A turn of this tab that ends upstairs leaves the octopus where it is. walkTo('blanket') still sets the app anchor to 'blanket' and resolves at once, because scene moveTo does not walk upstairs, so the state returns to idle with no walk, no hop and no step sound.

changes.what: Rewrote 5-3 and 5-5 and added 5-5c, 5-5d and 5-6. New helpers: track5/untrack5 (a per-frame record of frames downstairs, walk frames, distance moved and sleeping-while-up frames), seen5 (the scene's own projection is inside the scene and the screen) and blanket5.
changes.why: The old checks asserted the old move to the blanket. The new checks guard the new behaviour and the no-sleep-upstairs rule.
These weekly-gift lines had no failing check. RO-1 guards `+ (w.kept | 0)` in weekState's due. RO-2 guards the `d <= ek` bound in oldDone.

changes.what: §2 now has the OW-3 (b) decision (owner default 11-13) and OW-4 kept (owner default 11-13, the 11-08 rule). The §3.1 table and the awake-window note say the mirror opens its sheet for an octopus that stayed upstairs awake.
changes.why: These are the places where the 11-12 decisions are written.

changes.what: Same two decisions in the 11-11 loft note.
changes.why: The 11-12 decision text also lives here. docs/OWNER_DECISIONS.md has no 11-12 entries (the owner-lane commit a0483dd did not touch it), so I left it alone.

decisions:
Item 2, another tab's turn arriving after the window has passed: I kept today's move. The octopus is moved to the blanket and naps there (sleepNow, then restDown, then scene.octDown, with no walk, sound or log row). Keeping it awake upstairs would mean pretending to be awake an octopus whose nap is already due, which is not honest. A "walk down while the player watches" would need a new stair-walk animation in the scene and new behaviour, which is beyond the smallest change. The move happens in front of the player only in this rare case (a frozen or background tab that receives a stale storage event while the player is upstairs), and it is the same move as before the fix.

Where the blanket placement happens: in the app's on.octUp handler. octUnmountLoft already jumps the scene octopus to its own attic anchor and emits octUp(false, anchor), and every way out of the loft (the stairs, the play room or outside via showPlace, a ceremony start, finishing the salon) goes through it. A reload starts in the attic, where restKept and resumeRunning already place it. Doing it in the app keeps scene3d.js untouched, so the scene perf test was not needed.

Item 4, the mirror: openSalon works for an octopus that stays upstairs awake. In 5-3, tapping the mirror opens the sheet with zero asks and zero new rows, and no new line was added. I found no reason against it: the octopus is present and awake, which matches the existing table row "깨어 있는 틈 포함".

Item 5: the tap line still works upstairs. 5-3 checks that the bubble equals APP.tapLine().text with data-tap = 1.

Smaller choices:
- The earlier run dropped a `if (octWithMe()) octState('idle')` line in finalPose because it was equivalent: walkTo('blanket') upstairs resolves at once and the existing .then sets idle.
- The 5-5d "outside the window" case needs the storage event to be held back until the window has passed. A capture listener on window did not run before the app's earlier bubble listener in this Chromium (probe-ev.js in the scratch folder), so the test wraps addEventListener('storage') in an init script instead.
new_text: No new player-facing line or label. The tap line and the mirror sheet are the existing ones.

Docs only (Korean decision text): SALON.md §2 '위층에 따라 와 있는 채 차례가 끝나면 내가 내려갈 때까지 위층에 남는다 (주인 기본값 11-13, 검증 OW-3 (b) ...)' and '틈은 보는 다락에서만 센다 (주인 기본값 11-13, 검증 OW-4 — 11-08 규칙 그대로 ...)'; the same two in ROOM_EXPANSION.md line 625; SALON.md §3.1 '11-13: 따라 와 있던 채 차례가 끝나 위층에 남은 틈이면 시트가 열린다'.
guard:
Checks added or rewritten (scenario Z part 5, run with SMOKE_ONLY=Z SMOKE_Z=5; scenario Q, Q21):
- 5-3a: a stay-home turn ends while the octopus is upstairs (the brain's slow-turn hook). The octopus stays up, idle, in the awake phase, saved as 'sleep', with rest.away set. Every frame it is never down, never walking and never asleep upstairs, and it moves less than 0.001. Its projected position is inside the scene and the screen, it is visible with hop 0, and no step, door, ceremony, peek or salon sound plays.
- 5-3b: tapping it upstairs shows the tap line (APP.tapLine). The mirror opens the sheet with zero asks and zero new rows. rest.left does not change over 10 s upstairs.
- 5-3c: going down puts the scene octopus exactly on the blanket anchor, idle and awake, with rest.left >= 15000. Climbing again, it does not follow.
- 5-5 (inside the window): another tab finishes a turn while the octopus is upstairs here. It stays up and awake, with the same per-frame and in-view checks as 5-3a.
- 5-5c: reloading while it is upstairs in the window puts it on the blanket, awake, with at least 15000 ms left. Climbing again, it does not follow.
- 5-5d (outside the window): the other tab's storage event is held back until the window has passed. The octopus ends on the blanket asleep (phase 'nap') and is never asleep upstairs in any frame.
- 5-6: with __ppolAwakeMs = 0 and a turn ending while the octopus is upstairs, it ends asleep on the blanket with zero sleeping-upstairs frames.
- Q21 RO-1: same week, kept = 1, gift not claimed, the date hook moved to the next Monday, reload. Expect week.prev = {12, 2} and shells up by 12 + 3.
- Q21 RO-2: last week had only two visit days, four other tasks done, the slot never replaced. On Monday expect no week.prev and only the day gift.

left: When another tab's turn arrives after the window has passed while the player is upstairs (a frozen or background tab), the octopus still moves to the blanket in front of the player, as before. I kept this because the alternative is a sleeping octopus upstairs or one held awake past its nap. A visible walk down the stairs would need new scene work.

While the octopus is upstairs in its awake window, the window does not count down (OW-4, kept by owner default). If the player stays upstairs for a long time, it stays awake there until the 20-minute nap limit or a day change (napOver). After that, restPhase is 'up' and it is an ordinary awake octopus, so this is not a sleep-upstairs case.
docs/OWNER_DECISIONS.md was not updated. It holds no 11-12 entries; those decisions live in SALON.md §2 and ROOM_EXPANSION.md, where I wrote the 11-13 ones. The lead may want an index line there.
not_verified: The 2D fallback (?scene=2d): the loft and octUp exist only in the 3D scene. octWithMe() is false there, so the changed branches do nothing, but I did not run a 2D check for these paths.

Reaching the play room or outside directly from the loft during the awake window: this goes through octUnmountLoft and on.octUp by reading of the code, but there is no dedicated check for that route (the stairs and a reload are tested).

A ceremony starting while the octopus stays upstairs in its window (a new invite from upstairs): by reading of the code, octUnmountLoft and on.octUp place it on the blanket first, then the ceremony runs as before. Not tested by a check.

A day change while the octopus stays upstairs in its window: by the code, napOver makes lieDown clear the rest and leave it awake (not asleep), but there is no check for this exact combination. The existing 5-a check covers a day change for an octopus that did not follow.
No real model turn was run; the brain's slow-turn test hook stood in for it.
Y has one clean run on the final code, not a quiet-machine run.
